en: When working with the Codex desktop app,
there are a couple of features you should be
aware of, which you'll also see throughout
this course, but I also wanna mention them
right away. For one, you can add multiple
projects here, and then you can have
different threads across those different
projects, different sessions. And you can
also have multiple sessions running in
parallel so that you have multiple agents
working in parallel, multiple agents per
project, multiple agents across projects.
That's all possible. You also have your
settings and we'll take a look at some
specific settings throughout the course when
we need them, like for example, MCP servers,
but it's definitely worth exploring those
too. For example, here you can also
personalize how Codex behaves and this will
actually also affect how it behaves in the
CLI, but I will get back to that.
You can configure a code editor that should
be used by default so that you can click on
that to open a project in that code editor,
for example. Depending on which thread from
which project you had selected. You can
create Git commits here and also preview
changes. And again, these are all things
we'll explore in greater detail throughout
this course. And you also have a built-in
terminal which you can open up also with
that shortcut that shows up there on your
system so that if you wanna interact with
your project from the command line, you can
do that in addition to this interface. And
that's just a regular terminal, your default
system terminal, integrated in this app.
In this input box here, you cannot just
control which model to use and so on, but
you also have various slash commands
available. So if you type a slash, it
doesn't show up here. Instead, this menu
opens and there are various commands you can
invoke here.
Now, we'll take a look at plenty of them
throughout the course. We'll take a look at
forking and so on, but it's worth noting
that they are there and that here, for
example, you can see your current usage
status if you want to or provide feedback to
the OpenAI team and a bunch of other things.
You also have this button here, which allows
you to set up certain run actions. And if
you press this, you can simply define some
steps that should be executed when that
button is pressed. Like for example, you
could have this command for starting some
dev server.
You don't have to do that. You can run it in
the command line instead, but that can be a
convenient way of setting up such a command
which you can execute in a certain project.
And this is all scoped to the different
projects. And what you're editing here
simply depends on which thread from which
project you have selected. For the threads
in projects, you can also assign names to
them, archive them if you want to get rid of
them, or pin them to, well, have them pinned
here in the sidebar. You can of course also
do that with these buttons right here. That
is the archive button here.
And much more. As mentioned, we'll see all
these features throughout the course. This
is just a quick tour to get you started and
oriented in this desktop app.
